0.content:
AVERETH — WORLD IDENTITY [CANON]
The known world is dominated by one immense continent, Avereth, surrounded by ocean. Recorded history is extremely deep: civilizations, dynasties, religions and peoples have risen and vanished, and a few ancient beings remember eras ordinary people know only as legend.

The tone is high fantasy with contrast. Safe cities, farms, workshops, trade, families, festivals and ordinary careers coexist with dangerous wilderness, Monsters, natural Dungeons, political violence and ancient powers. The world is not uniformly grim and is not built as a sequence of combat zones.

Current established great powers are six human kingdoms — Valedorn Crown, Caelreth, Veyrhold, Solmere, Ilyrion and Duskreach — plus two recognized monster realms, the Ashen Scale Dominion and Verdant Fang Court. Human and monster states are not unified species blocs; trade, diplomacy, rivalry, war and cooperation can cross species lines.

Material culture is Western-fantasy medieval alongside mana and high magic. Modern or industrial technology is not the default.

1.comment: CORE — Canon, blank space, invention boundary
1.content:
AVERETH — CANON AND GENERATIVE SPACE [AUTHORING RULE]
This lorebook is narrator/world knowledge, not knowledge any NPC automatically has. Current Engine state, resolved mechanics, NPC knowledge boundaries and player agency always override it.

Blank space is intentional. When play needs a new person, place, custom, faction, Monster, Dungeon feature, historical event, Quest or Class/Evolution theme, invent it from established causes around it, at the scale the scene needs. New material becomes persistent canon only once it is established in play.

2.content:
CONTINENTAL GEOGRAPHY [CANON + GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Avereth is immense. Long travel between cities and kingdoms matters; settlements are not compressed together for convenience.

When creating new geography, derive it from connected causes:
1. LANDFORM/CLIMATE — coast, river basin, forest, highland, plain, marsh, badland, volcanic zone, etc.
2. RESOURCES/HAZARDS — water, farmland, timber, ore, mana phenomena, Monsters, storms, disease or difficult terrain.
3. MOVEMENT — roads, rivers, passes, ports, bridges and caravan routes form because people need them.
4. SETTLEMENT — towns grow where defense, trade, water, resources or administration justify them.
5. POLITICS — borders usually follow defensible terrain, old claims, roads, rivers, settlements or negotiated history.

Biomes should transition plausibly rather than appearing as isolated theme parks. Wilderness can be empty, productive, beautiful or dangerous without always containing a Quest hook. Exact unestablished borders, minor states, islands, rivers and regions remain open until play needs them.

3.content:
BEYOND AVERETH [OPEN CANON]
Avereth is the dominant known continent in the campaign's current scope. Oceans, islands and distant lands may exist, but no second great continent, overseas empire or hidden global civilization is established yet.

If play reaches beyond the known map, introduce distant geography gradually through credible contact: sailors, maps, trade goods, migrants, ruins, expeditions or direct travel. Do not retroactively make a newly invented overseas power responsible for established continental history without strong prior causes. New lands should expand the world rather than explain everything that already exists.

4.content:
HISTORICAL LAYERING [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Avereth has enough history for multiple unrelated eras to overlap. When inventing history, use:
PAST CAUSE -> MATERIAL OR INSTITUTIONAL REMNANT -> WHO CARES NOW.

A historical layer may leave roads, fortifications, tombs, changed borders, legal privileges, old feuds, loanwords, mixed populations, religious sites, abandoned infrastructure, artifacts or ecological damage. Most ruins are not world-ending secrets. Most old wars were fought for recognizable interests such as succession, territory, trade routes, faith, resources or security.

Avoid one universal precursor civilization that explains every mystery. Different regions should have different histories, and even well-known events can be remembered differently by courts, temples, scholars and local communities.

5.comment: WORLD — Culture and local identity scaffold
5.content:
CULTURE [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Generate culture from lived conditions rather than decorative stereotypes. For a new community, choose only a few relevant traits from climate and food; dominant work; trade connections; military pressure; religion; local law; family structure; architecture; holidays; dress; hospitality; attitudes toward magic, Monsters and Rank; speech or naming habits.

A realm is not a monoculture. Capital, frontier, coast, countryside, minority communities and occupational groups may differ while sharing broader institutions. Customs can be contested or changing.

Names should gain regional consistency through reuse of phonetic tendencies, titles, family-name habits and occupational bynames once established. Do not make every cultural trait mechanically significant.

6.content:
RELIGION AND BELIEF [CANON + GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Temples, healers, soul rites, pilgrimage traditions and ancient faiths exist in Avereth, especially visibly in Ilyrion. The setting does not currently define one mandatory universal pantheon or prove every theological claim.

New faiths may center on gods, spirits, ancestors, cosmic principles, historically powerful figures, saints, sacred places or philosophical traditions, but believers' claims do not become objective world truth merely because they state them.

For a local faith, generate: what it values; what practices express those values; what institution/community sustains it; what material role it plays; and one internal disagreement or limitation. Temples can own property, teach, heal, arbitrate, preserve records or wield political influence, but authority depends on local law and established power.

7.content:
LAW AND AUTHORITY [CANON + GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Local rulers, civic authorities, courts, guards, militaries, landholders and customary institutions govern ordinary law. The Adventurers' Guild does not replace them.

When a legal issue matters, identify which authority actually has jurisdiction; what conduct is prohibited or owed; who can investigate, arrest, judge or collect; how status, evidence, Rank and local custom affect procedure; and what realistic limits constrain enforcement.

Law should create consequences and negotiation, not omniscient policing. Powerful individuals may be difficult to arrest, but Rank does not automatically erase property rights, contracts, local politics or social retaliation.

8.content:
CURRENCY / EVERYDAY ECONOMY [CANON]
Common currency uses whole coins: 10 Copper = 1 Silver; 10 Silver = 1 Gold. There is no standard fractional Copper.

Prices are intentionally contextual rather than globally fixed. Cost should reflect local supply, demand, danger, transport, quality, scarcity, law and bargaining position. Legal trade can include food, lodging, transport, tools, Gear, magical services, Skill Stones, Monster/Dungeon materials, healing, training, maps and information.

Wealth is uneven. A valuable reward should come from a giver who can plausibly afford it or from property/resources that actually exist. Do not inflate every adventuring job into treasure-scale economics.

9.content:
MATERIAL CULTURE / TRAVEL / COMMUNICATION [CANON]
Ordinary Avereth life is pre-industrial: handcraft, smithing, mills, farms, carts, horses, sailing vessels, fortified settlements, markets and written records. Mana and high magic can exceed mundane medieval capability, but they have not produced a default modern industrial society.

Ordinary long-distance communication uses letters, messengers, couriers and travelers. Magical long-distance communication can exist through powerful magic, institutions or artifacts, but is not universal on-demand infrastructure.

Ordinary travel is by foot, mount, wagon/carriage and ship. Distance consumes meaningful time. Teleportation or comparable transport may exist when explicitly established but is never assumed to be common public transit. Do not introduce firearms, engines, railways, electrical grids, telephones, computers or mass industrial production without explicit later canon.

10.content:
MANA IN ORDINARY LIFE [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Mana is normal to Avereth, but access, training and power are uneven. Minor magic can coexist with medieval institutions without turning every household into a modern utility network.

When inventing a practical magical service, ask:
SOURCE — who supplies the Skill, ritual, artifact or mana?
COST — training, materials, time, risk or money?
SCALE — household, workshop, city institution or rare specialist?
LIMIT — why has this not replaced every mundane alternative?

Use magic to enrich professions and institutions rather than erase logistics. A magical lamp, healer, ward, messenger method or enchanted tool can be common in one place and scarce elsewhere if economics and training justify it.

11.content:
DEATH / RESURRECTION [CANON]
Death is socially real and normally permanent. Powerful temples or specialists can sometimes perform rare, extremely expensive soul-return rituals through high magic, but resurrection is not routine medical care and ordinary people cannot assume access.

Exact ritual limits, prices and eligibility remain undefined until relevant. Do not use resurrection to erase ordinary consequences or create casual revolving-door mortality. Mechanical revival requires an explicit established mechanic.

12.content:
RANK / LEVEL / EVOLUTION [CANON]
Ordinary society broadly understands Level, Rank, Class, Skills, Skill Proficiency and Evolution. Exact Levels require measurement, commonly through Guild or temple methods; exact Core Stat numbers are not normally visible.

Standard Rank milestones follow Class Evolution every 15 Levels:
F — Base stage, Levels 1-14.
E — first evolution, starting Level 15.
D — second evolution, starting Level 30.
C — third evolution, starting Level 45.
B — Half-Divine stage, starting Level 60.
A — higher Transcendent stage, starting Level 75.
S — Full-Divine stage, starting Level 90.

These are power/evolution bands, not moral or social titles. Rare paths may differ only when explicit content establishes an exception.

13.content:
EVOLUTION / LIFESPAN / SOCIAL POWER [CANON]
Evolution improves health and longevity as well as power. Broad natural lifespans are tendencies:
F ~100-120 years; E ~150-180; D ~250-350; C ~500-700; B ~2,000-3,000; A ~10,000-20,000; S 100,000+.

Most people remain F/E. D-ranks are respected specialists or local elites; C-ranks are major regional figures; B-ranks often occupy senior institutional roles. A-ranks are rare strategic figures. S-ranks are kingdom-level deterrents.

High Rank creates leverage, not universal obedience. Politics, legitimacy, loyalty, institutions and coalitions still matter. Exact high-rank populations remain uncertain because independents and hidden individuals exist.

14.content:
CLASS FRAMEWORK [CANON]
A Class is a major power path, not an absolute prohibition on learning outside Skills. The current standard Base Classes are:
Warrior — favored STR/VIT; direct martial offense with defensive depth.
Mage — favored INT/WIL; arcane offense, wards, mobility and control.
Guardian — favored VIT/WIL; protection, endurance and battlefield holding.
Duelist — favored STR/AGI; precision, mobility, tempo and counterplay.
Ranger — favored AGI/PER; ranged precision, positioning and hunting-oriented play.

Skills remain open-learn when a legitimate source exists. Class Affinity affects learning/proficiency speed rather than directly multiplying damage.

Later Class Evolutions are NOT a fixed prewritten tree. They emerge from actual development.

15.content:
CLASS EVOLUTION — GENERATION BODY [CANON FRAME + CREATIVE SCAFFOLD]
Standard milestones are Levels 15/30/45/60/75/90 for E/D/C/B/A/S. At a milestone, generate 2-4 plausible options from ESTABLISHED development rather than a hidden fixed menu.

Build each option from:
1. ROOT — current Base Class and prior Evolutions.
2. EVIDENCE — repeated Skills/elements, weapon style, stat investment, combat role, training, discoveries, major victories and meaningful choices.
3. THESIS — one clear direction the path deepens.
4. TRADE-OFF — what the path emphasizes and what it does not solve.
5. CONTINUITY — existing Skills remain recognizable unless explicitly transformed.
6. MECHANICAL SEED — at most one coherent new passive/permission/trait at a standard evolution; exact mechanics must follow Core/Content design rules.
7. NAME — concise fantasy title derived from function, method, element, weapon, ethos or earned identity.
8. RARITY — rare Evolutions require rare ESTABLISHED conditions, not random rarity.

Do not grant extra universal HP/stat growth unless explicit mechanics say so. Once chosen, the Evolution becomes fixed canon.

16.content:
WARRIOR — EVOLUTION SEED BODY [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Core identity: direct martial force, weapon commitment, pressure and effectiveness under resistance. Favored Stats are STR/VIT.

Plausible axes include aggression/finishing power; mastery of a repeatedly used weapon family; momentum and line-breaking; vanguard endurance and formation fighting; counter-force or guard-breaking; disciplined defense; or command only if leadership has actually been established.

Build from observed behavior. A Warrior who repeatedly protects others should not receive the same options as one who specializes in overwhelming single-target offense. Weapon-specific Evolutions require actual weapon history.

17.content:
MAGE — EVOLUTION SEED BODY [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Core identity: deliberate arcane shaping through INT/WIL, with ranged magic, wards, mobility and control.

Plausible axes include a repeatedly developed element/damage expression; arcane structure, efficiency or barriers; battlefield control/spatial manipulation; mobility/casting under pressure; ritual/research specialization if established through study; or hybridization only when a second discipline has genuinely developed.

Do not assign an elemental identity because one spell was used once. Specialization should reflect sustained practice, teachers, discoveries, Skill choices or major events.

18.content:
GUARDIAN — EVOLUTION SEED BODY [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Core identity: VIT/WIL-driven protection, holding space, survival and creating safety under pressure.

Plausible axes include personal durability/attrition; protecting allies or civilians; retaliation for attacking protected space; shield/armor mastery when actually used; interception/denial; or magical warding if established.

The evolution should answer HOW this Guardian protects, not simply 'more defense'. A solitary endurance specialist, bodyguard and battlefield anchor should develop differently.

19.content:
DUELIST — EVOLUTION SEED BODY [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Core identity: STR/AGI precision, tempo, mobility, deception and exploiting narrow openings.

Plausible axes include extreme precision/weak-point play; mobility and disengagement; counters/parries/reactive timing; feints and tempo manipulation; repeated weapon-style specialization; or multi-hit pressure if consistently developed.

Evolution should grow from fighting behavior rather than cosmetic elegance. A counter-focused Duelist should not automatically become a speed path.

20.content:
RANGER — EVOLUTION SEED BODY [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Core identity: AGI/PER precision, ranged control, positioning and exploiting information about terrain and targets.

Plausible axes include long-range marksmanship and deliberate high-value shots; mobile archery/skirmishing; hunting, tracking and target study; battlefield suppression or multi-target pressure; specialized ammunition or bow technique if legitimately learned; wilderness expertise only when actually developed.

Do not make 'Ranger' automatically mean druid, animal companion, forest mystic or nature magic. Those are possible later developments only if established. Alaric's future Ranger Evolutions should derive from his real Skills, stat investment, tactics, teachers, hunts and discoveries.

21.content:
SKILLS / TRAINING / LEARNING [CANON]
Formal Skills are commonly learned through teachers, Skill Stones, rewards/Evolution, established self-development or another legitimate source. Experimentation alone is not the normal route for most people.

Skills are not absolutely class-exclusive. A Class provides affinities and a natural direction; cross-discipline learning is possible but may be slower or require access.

Known Skills develop through meaningful use and training. Safe repetition without challenge should not magically generate mastery. High proficiency can make a Skill eligible for later Skill Evolution, which should remain recognizably descended from how that technique was actually used and trained.

Exact Skill mechanics, numerical balance and proficiency calculations belong to Engine/Core/Content.

22.content:
EDUCATION AND ACCESS [CANON + GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Schools and specialist academies exist. Nobles, wealthy families, militaries, temples, Adventurer families and scholarship students generally have better access to teachers, rare Skill Stones, records and safe training.

Avereth does not normally use cultivation-style Sects. Similar social functions may be filled by great houses, royal lines, temples, military lineages, academies and old magical families.

Access creates social geography: a provincial fighter may know practical techniques but lack rare instruction; a wealthy academy may have theory but demand fees, service, patronage or examinations. Knowledge should have owners and transmission paths rather than appear whenever the protagonist needs it.

23.content:
DOMAINS [CANON WORLD LORE]
B-rank/Half-Divine development can manifest a personal Domain: an active authority field tied to the evolved Class or creature path. A Domain is qualitatively different from an ordinary Skill and is a major public marker of transcendent power.

Exact combat rules and modifiers are Engine-owned. Narratively, lower-rank people and institutions treat active Domains with extreme seriousness. Equivalent Domain users can contest one another without a universal 'higher score wins' rule.

A player's specific Domain Law should emerge from the established evolution path and earlier passive/development, not a random cosmic title. High-Rank status should feel qualitatively important without becoming omniscience, automatic political authority or consequence-free behavior.

24.content:
HIGH-RANK DETERRENCE [CANON]
S-ranks are strategic actors, not routine battlefield units. Direct clashes risk catastrophic collateral damage and escalation, so they usually act through deterrence, diplomacy, representatives or intervention only when stakes justify it. B/A-ranks handle much of practical high-level conflict.

A powerful ruler or ancient being does not intervene merely because an unrelated lower-rank member of the same species or faction was harmed. High-rank actors have priorities, limited attention, political constraints and reasons to avoid escalation.

25.content:
QUEST GENERATION — CAUSAL RULE [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
A Quest is not content vending. It begins because someone or some institution wants the world to be different from how it is now.

Before generating a Quest, establish:
CAUSE — what current condition created the need?
STAKEHOLDER — who cares, and why?
KNOWLEDGE — how does the giver know there is a problem?
CAPABILITY GAP — why does the giver need outside help?
DESIRED STATE — what would count as success?
MEANS — what reward, authority, information or access can the giver realistically provide?

Generate Quests from existing people, places, shortages, threats, obligations, trade, politics, ecology, previous outcomes and newly established local conditions. Do not manufacture a crisis simply because Alaric is present.

GUILD BOARD MINIMUMS do not mean every new listing must be a fresh emergency. A branch can maintain its required pool through routine standing work, escorts, surveys, deliveries, material procurement, pest control, training support, investigation, repair/security work and regional-network contracts. The board should feel economically and institutionally plausible rather than like five catastrophes per Rank per day.

26.content:
QUEST MOTIVATION BODY [RESEARCH-INFORMED SCAFFOLD]
Use one primary giver motivation to keep a generated Quest intentional:
KNOWLEDGE — learn, verify, map, study, spy, interview.
COMFORT — remove a nuisance, obtain necessities/luxuries, restore ordinary function.
REPUTATION — prove status, recover face, obtain/display something prestigious.
SERENITY/JUSTICE — resolve a grievance, find a missing person, recover what was lost, settle an unresolved wrong.
PROTECTION — guard, rescue, treat, repair, fortify, prevent a threat.
CONQUEST — defeat/displace an opponent, seize an objective, sabotage hostile capability.
WEALTH — gather resources, secure trade, recover valuables, create something saleable.
ABILITY — train, test, practice, research, acquire instruction/tools for mastery.
EQUIPMENT — obtain, repair, improve, replace or recover a useful asset.

These are generation categories, not in-world labels. The giver speaks from actual circumstances.

28.content:
QUEST ACTION GRAMMAR [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Build a Quest from a short chain of atomic world actions rather than a monologue of plot.

GO/REACH — travel to a person/place.
FIND/OBSERVE/SPY/SURVEY — acquire evidence.
TALK/LISTEN/NEGOTIATE/REPORT — social information exchange.
GET/BUY/GATHER/TAKE/RECOVER — obtain an external object/resource.
GIVE/DELIVER/EXCHANGE — transfer it.
USE/REPAIR/TREAT/BUILD — change an object/person/place.
DEFEND/ESCORT/RESCUE/CAPTURE — protect or control a moving actor.
ATTACK/DEFEAT/DRIVE OFF/SABOTAGE — overcome active opposition.

A high-level action may naturally contain a subproblem when current world conditions require it. Do not add subquests merely to lengthen a Quest. This grammar describes possible objectives, never actions automatically chosen for Alaric.

29.content:
COMPLETE QUEST BODY [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
When a new tracked Quest is actually offered, silently ensure it has:

1. TITLE — practical and locally meaningful.
2. GIVER — a real person/institution with authority or stake.
3. CAUSE — the existing problem/opportunity.
4. MOTIVE — why the giver cares.
5. DESIRED END STATE — what completion means.
6. QUEST RANK — for Guild contracts: Novice / Proven / Veteran / Elite / Master / Grandmaster / Legend. Private work has no Quest Rank unless the Guild lists it.
7. OBJECTIVE PATH — normally 1-4 meaningful steps; more only when fiction supports it.
8. ACCESS/KNOWLEDGE — what the player is told and what remains unknown.
9. COMPLETION EVIDENCE — how the giver can know the task is done.
10. REWARD SOURCE — why the reward exists and who can provide it.
11. CONSEQUENCE — what changes on success, failure, refusal or delay when relevant.

Do not pre-author every branch. Let branches emerge from player decisions and changing world state.

ENGINE NOTE:
The <avereth> fact report still carries the Quest's hidden level (the Engine's Quest XP basis: the Level the task suits; for a Guild contract it lies inside its Quest Rank's band) and its type (minor/standard/dangerous/major scope). Never show a Recommended Level in the story, on a board or in an NPC's words; the Guild speaks in Quest Ranks.

30.content:
GUILD QUEST RANK CALIBRATION [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]

Guild Quest Rank is an institutional assessment of the responsibility, danger, uncertainty and expected capability of a contract:
NOVICE — routine local work, low institutional risk, ordinary early-career contracts.
PROVEN — established professional work with meaningful danger, uncertainty or responsibility.
VETERAN — serious professional assignments where reliable independent judgment is expected.
ELITE — high-risk or high-consequence contracts requiring exceptional competence.
MASTER — Half-Divine/B-rank-scale institutional work; rare and regionally significant.
GRANDMASTER — A-rank-scale strategic contracts; very rare and usually regional/international.
LEGEND — S-rank-scale strategic matters; exceptional, not ordinary local board filler.

Quest Rank belongs to the Guild's contract system. It does NOT alter the actual world to match the adventurer, and a listed Quest may prove easier, harder or differently complicated than expected because Guild information can be incomplete.

Do not use a public "Recommended Level" field in Guild presentation. The person's Power Rank and Guild Rank remain separate from Quest Rank.

31.content:
QUEST REWARD BODY [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Rewards should come from the giver's means and motive. Possible rewards include coin, ordinary or rare goods, training, a Skill Stone, information, legal access, introductions, transport, lodging, healing, material rights, institutional favor or reputation.

Reward value should reflect scope, danger, scarcity and local economics. Not every Quest needs a magical item. A poor village may offer food, shelter, favors or pooled coin; a wealthy Guild office or noble can fund more.

Keep physical rewards external until actually transferred. Combat loot is separate from Quest payment. The Engine owns Quest XP and Level progression; never substitute a guessed XP amount.

32.content:
QUEST COMPLICATION BODY [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
A Quest does not require a twist. When a complication is justified, choose at most one or two that follow from the world: incomplete/wrong information; a moving target; conflicting stakeholders; legal restrictions; rival claimants; weather/terrain; resource shortage; time pressure already caused by events; collateral risk; changing Monster behavior; a damaged route; moral uncertainty; a third party pursuing its own goal.

Complications should reveal the world rather than invalidate prior facts. Avoid habitual betrayals, secret cults, hidden chosen-one connections and 'the real villain was the giver' as default twists.

33.content:
QUEST BRANCHING [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Branches arise from changing world state, not a prewritten dialogue tree. Useful outcome classes include: success as requested; success by another legitimate method; partial success; target escapes; evidence is incomplete; stakeholder refuses terms; a rival acts first; player abandons/refuses; the underlying situation changes.

Preserve consequences. A repaired bridge stays repaired until something changes it; a rescued NPC can later act from that history; an ignored threat may worsen, move, resolve without Alaric or be handled by someone else.

Never force Alaric onto a branch. Present the world and let his choices determine which state occurs.

34.comment: GUILD — Adventurers' Guild and rank systems
34.content:
ADVENTURERS' GUILD — INSTITUTION AND RANK SYSTEMS [CANON]
The Adventurers' Guild is a neutral transnational institution for registration, certification, contracts, Monster/Dungeon information, rewards, material brokerage, frontier support and high-rank mediation. It does not replace rulers, courts, guards, militaries or property law.

POWER RANK and GUILD RANK are different systems.
Power Rank F / E / D / C / B / A / S is a person's objective Evolution state; it exists with or without Guild membership, and the Guild cannot grant it.
Guild Rank Novice / Proven / Veteran / Elite / Master / Grandmaster / Legend is institutional standing held only by registered members.
Standard correspondence: F -> Novice, E -> Proven, D -> Veteran, C -> Elite, B -> Master, A -> Grandmaster, S -> Legend. It is a promotion minimum, not identity: an E-rank member may still be Novice, and a non-member has no Guild Rank.

Guild contracts carry a Quest Rank with the same labels (the Guild's assessment of responsibility, danger and expected capability). Members normally take contracts of their own Guild Rank and below.

35.content:
NON-GUILD WORK [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Not all meaningful work passes through the Adventurers' Guild. Local rulers, guards, temples, merchants, caravans, craftspeople, scholars, families, villages, military officers and other adventurers can create requests/contracts when they have a real need.

Form should match the giver: a guard captain issues an official task; a merchant negotiates terms; a villager may ask informally; a temple may frame service as duty or charity. Jurisdiction, proof and reward depend on the source.

Guild Rank labels are institutional Guild terminology. Private work does not automatically acquire a Guild Quest Rank unless the Guild evaluates or lists it. If the Engine needs a hidden internal difficulty/scope value, that is an implementation detail rather than world-facing Guild lore.

36.content:
SETTLEMENT GENERATION BODY [CREATIVE SCAFFOLD]
Create only as much of a settlement as the scene needs. Anchor it with:
PURPOSE — why people live here: farming, route, port, mine, administration, fortress, pilgrimage, craft, frontier support, etc.
SITE — water, terrain and defenses.
ECONOMY — 1-3 major livelihoods and what must be imported.
AUTHORITY — who governs and what their practical reach is.
PRESSURE — one current problem or tension, which may be mundane.
TEXTURE — a few sensory/architectural traits derived from realm and climate.
CONNECTIONS — road/river/port and nearby places it actually depends on.

Districts, named officials, histories and secrets remain blank until relevant. A settlement should feel like a place where people live, not a bundle of quest markers.

37.content:
ORGANIZATION GENERATION BODY [CREATIVE SCAFFOLD]
For a new organization, define:
PURPOSE — what it exists to accomplish.
RESOURCE — money, knowledge, land, force, legitimacy, magic, trade or social trust.
MEMBERSHIP — who joins and why.
AUTHORITY — what it can actually compel.
PUBLIC FACE — how outsiders encounter it.
INTERNAL PRESSURE — one disagreement, dependency or institutional limit.
RELATIONS — only relevant allies/rivals rooted in interests.

Organizations are not hive minds. Individual members can disagree. Avoid creating a continent-wide secret organization for a local scene unless prior causes support that scale.

38.content:
NPC GENERATION BODY [CREATIVE SCAFFOLD]
Most NPCs should begin as people with a life, not content dispensers. Generate:
ROLE — occupation/social position.
OBLIGATION — what they need to be doing today.
STAKE — what they care about in the current situation.
KNOWLEDGE SOURCE — why they know what they know.
LIMIT — time, money, authority, skill, fear, loyalty or ignorance.
VOICE — one restrained social/linguistic cue.

Only add deeper secrets, family, ambition or recurring significance when interaction earns it. An NPC may remain background. Never give NPCs knowledge merely because the narrator has it.

39.content:
MONSTER ECOLOGY / FAUNA [CANON]
Native non-sapient fauna are part of Avereth's Monster ecology. Familiar animal-shaped creatures such as wolves, deer, horses, boars, bears and birds are mechanically Monsters with Level and Rank even when peaceful, domesticated or ecologically ordinary. 'Animal' remains normal everyday language for ecology/body type; it is not a separate rules category.

Monster classification does NOT mean hostility. Monsters are natural populations: they reproduce, compete, migrate, form territories/social structures, are hunted or domesticated, and may evolve through Ranks. Most ordinary fauna near settlements are F-rank; evolved higher-rank specimens become progressively rarer and more dangerous.

Sapience is separate from Monster classification. Some Monsters speak, organize societies, rule territory and conduct diplomacy.

40.content:
MONSTER SPECIES GENERATION BODY [CREATIVE SCAFFOLD]
For a new Monster species, begin with ecology before powers:
BODY PLAN — use the nearest established mechanical anchor; narration does not invent stats.
HABITAT — where it can actually live.
DIET/ENERGY — what sustains it.
BEHAVIOR — solitary, herd, pack, territorial, migratory, nesting, parasitic, etc.
PRESSURE — predators, prey, season, people, Dungeon influence or mana conditions.
ADAPTATION — 1-2 visible traits that make sense for that ecology.
HUMAN RELATION — ignored, hunted, farmed, feared, traded, protected, sacred, nuisance, etc.

Higher Rank may transform a species, but do not give every specimen exotic abilities. Rare evolved individuals should feel like developments of the base ecology unless explicit magic creates a true mutation.

41.content:
SAPIENT MONSTER SOCIETIES [GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Intelligent Monsters are not automatically humans with cosmetic bodies, nor automatically enemies. Build social forms from species needs, lifespan, territory, reproduction, power distribution, trade and history.

A polity can use lineage, councils, personal dominance, oaths, territory, ritual, bureaucracy or other institutions when those forms make sense. Different species can share states or compete within them. Individual Monsters vary in loyalty and temperament just as humans do.

Avoid treating one hostile encounter as evidence that an entire species or realm is hostile.

42.content:
NATURAL DUNGEONS [CANON]
Natural Dungeons are persistent supernatural ecosystems/resource zones shaped by concentrated mana and other established local conditions. They can contain unusual environments, rare materials, Skill Stones and exceptional Monsters.

A Dungeon is a physical world location, not a temporary game instance that appears for Alaric. It can be known, owned, disputed, exploited, sealed, partially mapped or ecologically connected to the surrounding region.

Exact layouts, ownership and local history remain open until established.

43.content:
DUNGEON GENERATION BODY [CREATIVE SCAFFOLD]
Create a Dungeon from five connected layers:
ORIGIN/CONDITION — what mana/geological/historical condition sustains it.
ECOLOGY — what lives there and how food/energy/material cycles work.
STRUCTURE — natural caverns, ruins, warped terrain, constructed zones or mixtures, with spatial logic.
VALUE — materials, Skill Stones, research, strategic position or another reason people enter.
CLAIMS — who maps, harvests, guards, owns, avoids or contests it.
CHANGE — what currently makes this visit different, if anything.

Difficulty should vary by depth/zone and established ecology, not automatically match Alaric. Puzzles, locked doors and bosses require an in-world reason. Do not populate every room with combat.

44.content:
LOOT / MATERIAL GENERATION BODY [CREATIVE SCAFFOLD]
External loot should have a source and physical existence. For a new material/item establish only what is needed:
SOURCE — corpse, plant, mineral, workshop, cache, Dungeon, owner.
FORM — what can physically be carried/harvested.
USE — craft, food, alchemy, ritual, trade, tool, trophy, etc.
MARKET — who values it and why.
RARITY — local abundance versus scarcity.
OWNERSHIP/RISK — whether taking it is lawful, contested or dangerous.

Do not auto-pick up, harvest, sell or convert objects into Coin. Generic Gear does not acquire a legendary maker, hidden faction mark or ancient provenance without a real cause.

45.content:
RUMORS / UNCERTAIN INFORMATION [CREATIVE SCAFFOLD]
A rumor is a claim with a source, not automatic truth. Generate rumors from what people could plausibly observe, misunderstand, exaggerate or repeat.

Useful uncertainty includes partial observation, competing interpretations, stale information, institutional bias, or a true observation paired with a false explanation.

Do not use rumors to repair an NPC knowledge leak after the fact. Engine knowledge/claim state remains authoritative.

46.content:
LIVING-WORLD EVENT BODY [CREATIVE SCAFFOLD]
Events should emerge from existing causes: weather, schedules, trade, migration, politics, obligations, ongoing threats, resource shortages, institutional decisions or established NPC agendas.

Ask: what actor/process causes this; why now; who notices; what changes if Alaric does nothing?

Many changes should be mundane or off-screen. Do not manufacture an attack, secret, stranger, prophecy or clue merely to keep every scene busy. Quiet time is valid. Events do not need to involve Alaric, and ignored threads can resolve without him.

47.content:
CONFLICT GENERATION BODY [CREATIVE SCAFFOLD]
Create conflict from incompatible interests, not automatic good/evil factions. Identify the RESOURCE/RIGHT at stake; ACTORS; what each side believes; what each can actually do; why compromise has failed so far; and what would change the balance.

Scale conflict to its cause. A farm dispute stays local unless institutions escalate it. A border incident should not summon S-ranks by default. Leave room for negotiation, stalemate, third-party interests and unintended consequences.

48.content:
TRAVEL / ROUTE GENERATION BODY [CREATIVE SCAFFOLD]
Travel scenes should arise from the route: terrain, weather, traffic, tolls, repairs, inns, ferries, patrols, merchants, pilgrims, migrants, livestock, Monster ecology and local security.

Most travel events need not become Quests or fights. Mix uneventful progress, atmospheric evidence of the region, mundane interactions and occasional meaningful complications. Encounter frequency should reflect how busy and dangerous the route is, not the need to entertain Alaric every turn.

49.content:
KNOWLEDGE PROVENANCE [CREATIVE SCAFFOLD]
Useful information should have a path. Before an NPC or institution supplies specialized knowledge, establish why it has access: profession, direct experience, archive, teacher, witness, investigation, public record, local tradition or credible contact.

Experts can be wrong outside their field. Records can be incomplete or outdated. Rare Evolution conditions, hidden Dungeon details and high-rank secrets should have restricted provenance rather than being common tavern knowledge.

50.content:
CURRENT GREAT-POWER MAP [CANON]
Human kingdoms: Valedorn Crown, Caelreth, Veyrhold, Solmere, Ilyrion, Duskreach.
Recognized monster realms: Ashen Scale Dominion, Verdant Fang Court.
The Adventurers' Guild is neutral and transnational rather than a state.

Additional states, minor polities, city-states, noble holdings and independent high-rank actors may exist. Exact borders and histories remain open until established. There is no permanent human-versus-monster bloc.

51.content:
VALEDORN CROWN [CANON + REGIONAL SEED]
Position: central Avereth. Capital: Crownheart. Strongest human kingdom. Public S-ranks: 3.

Valedorn is a political center of human diplomacy with deep noble lineages, wealthy academies, old military institutions and one of the largest Adventurers' Guild headquarters. Its strength is breadth: population, wealth, administration, magic, military organization and diplomacy rather than one narrow specialty.

GENERATION FLAVOR: portray layered institutions, patronage, old rights, busy roads, provincial differences and court influence without making every scene court politics. Wealth and sophistication coexist with ordinary villages and practical local problems. Valedorn is powerful but coalitions can constrain it.

52.content:
CAELRETH [CANON + REGIONAL SEED]
Position: western Avereth. Capital: Asterhall. Top-tier human kingdom. Public S-ranks: 2.

Caelreth is the most academically arcane human kingdom, known for magical colleges, Skill-Stone study, enchantment research, ritual theory and old mage families. Powerful lineages guard rare Evolution knowledge. Relations with the Verdant Fang Court are cautious but can be scholarly and commercial.

GENERATION FLAVOR: education, research access, intellectual prestige, rival schools, protected techniques, specialist crafts and the economic cost of advanced magic. Do not turn every citizen into a Mage or every village into a laboratory.

53.content:
VEYRHOLD [CANON + REGIONAL SEED]
Position: eastern Avereth. Capital: Ironward. Top-tier martial kingdom. Public S-ranks: 2.

Veyrhold is heavily militarized and shaped by dangerous borders. Martial training, disciplined officer corps, fortified cities and Monster-hunting traditions are central. Its most openly tense great-power relationship is with the Ashen Scale Dominion, though both avoid escalation into direct S-rank war.

GENERATION FLAVOR: fortification, logistics, readiness, veteran culture, border economies and social weight of service. Military presence should vary by location; civilians still trade, farm, marry, argue and live ordinary lives.

54.content:
SOLMERE [CANON + REGIONAL SEED]
Position: southern coast. Capital: Goldharbor. Major human kingdom. Public S-ranks: 1.

Solmere is Avereth's largest maritime trade power. Ports, shipyards, merchant houses, mercenary contracts, Dungeon imports and inter-kingdom commerce dominate its politics. It can buy expertise and logistics at great scale and trades pragmatically across human and monster polities.

GENERATION FLAVOR: contracts, shipping, port diversity, warehouses, guilds, credit/trust networks, sailors, foreign goods and commercial law. Money creates influence but does not automatically solve military or high-rank problems.

55.content:
ILYRION [CANON + REGIONAL SEED]
Position: south-central riverlands. Capital: Sanctum Vale. Major human kingdom. Public S-ranks: 1.

Ilyrion is famous for temples, healers, soul rites, pilgrimage routes and religious scholarship. Many renowned resurrection specialists train or serve here. It is not a theocracy, though temples have major political and economic influence.

GENERATION FLAVOR: river travel, pilgrimage traffic, archives, hospitals/healers, religious institutions with differing doctrines and secular authorities negotiating with them. Faith should be plural and internally varied, not one unified church.

56.content:
DUSKREACH [CANON + REGIONAL SEED]
Position: southeastern marches. Capital: Blackgate. Regional human kingdom. Public S-ranks: none.

Duskreach is a hard frontier realm with strong B/A-rank military figures but no known Full-Divine protector. It survives through fortifications, alliances, Guild contracts, mercenary service and careful diplomacy with stronger neighbors.

GENERATION FLAVOR: practical frontier communities, repaired walls, guarded roads, local strongholds, negotiated protection, mercenaries and awareness of limited resources. Do not make the realm universally poor, lawless or bleak; frontier trade and ordinary prosperity can exist where security holds.

57.content:
ASHEN SCALE DOMINION [CANON + REGIONAL SEED]
Position: volcanic eastern highlands. Seat: Cinder Throne. Strongest recognized monster realm. Public S-ranks: 3.

The Dominion is ruled by ancient draconic and scaled bloodlines alongside other fire- and mountain-adapted monster species. Strength, bloodline, territory, oath and personal authority matter more than human-style bureaucracy. Some rulers think in centuries.

GENERATION FLAVOR: oath networks, territorial rights, old lineages, volcanic resources, long memory and personal authority. The Dominion is not uniformly evil or permanently at war with humans. Trade, negotiation and internal rivalry are possible.

58.content:
VERDANT FANG COURT [CANON + REGIONAL SEED]
Position: ancient western forests. Seat: Thornheart. Top-tier monster realm. Public S-ranks: 2.

The Court is a loose ancient polity of powerful beast lineages, transformed predators, forest spirits and other intelligent woodland species. Status is negotiated through territory, lineage, favors, challenges and old pacts rather than a human-style crown.

GENERATION FLAVOR: overlapping territorial claims, ritualized challenges, ecological obligations, lineage memory and negotiated access. Relations with Caelreth include trade, magical research, territorial disputes and occasional cooperation.

59.content:
ALDERWATCH [CANON SEED]
A walled city in Valedorn Crown and a possible campaign starting city. Exact districts, economy, rulers and history are intentionally open.

GENERATION DIRECTION: let Alderwatch reflect central Valedorn — connected roads, layered civic/noble authority and access to the wider kingdom — while giving it one local economic purpose and one local pressure only when play needs them. Do not prefill the city with plot-critical institutions.

60.content:
GLASSMERE [CANON SEED]
A walled city in Caelreth and a possible campaign starting city. Exact local details remain open.

GENERATION DIRECTION: allow visible contact with Caelreth's academic and magical economy — students, specialists, enchanted services, record-keeping or Skill-Stone trade where plausible — but keep ordinary crafts, neighborhoods and non-magical life present. Invent only institutions relevant to the current scene.

61.content:
REDMARCH [CANON SEED]
A walled city in Veyrhold and a possible campaign starting city. Exact local details remain open.

GENERATION DIRECTION: make fortification, military traffic, hunting expertise or frontier logistics visible without turning the whole city into a barracks. Local economy and current border pressures should be established only when relevant.

62.content:
TIDECROSS [CANON SEED]
A walled city in Solmere and a possible campaign starting city. Exact local details remain open.

GENERATION DIRECTION: give the city a credible relationship to maritime or river/coastal trade, contracts and movement of goods. Keep docks, markets or merchant activity proportional to what is actually established; not every Solmere settlement is Goldharbor.

63.content:
LUMENFORD [CANON SEED]
A walled city in Ilyrion and a possible campaign starting city. Exact local details remain open.

GENERATION DIRECTION: riverland travel, temples, healers, pilgrims or scholarship may be visible where relevant, alongside ordinary civic life. Do not assume every local priest knows resurrection or every resident is devout.

64.content:
ASHBRIDGE [CANON SEED]
A walled city in Duskreach and a possible campaign starting city. Exact districts, officials, industries and history remain open.

GENERATION DIRECTION: it should feel like a functioning frontier city in a realm without an S-rank protector: practical defenses, guarded approaches, people accustomed to risk, trade and hired expertise. Balance hardness with ordinary life. Establish specific industries, tensions and institutions only when play needs them.

65.content:
GUILD PROMOTION AND PLACEMENT [CANON]
To advance one Guild Rank a member must (1) possess at least the Power Rank corresponding to the TARGET Guild Rank and (2) have completed at least FIVE Guild Quests of their CURRENT Guild Rank. Example: Novice -> Proven requires E-rank plus 5 completed Novice Quests; Proven -> Veteran requires D-rank plus 5 Proven Quests. Evolution alone does not raise Guild Rank; the Quest count alone never bypasses the Power Rank.

LATE ENTRY: a newcomer whose Power Rank and verified experience exceed Novice may take a formal placement examination. Passing it can waive the completed-Quest requirement for the initial placement, but never the Power-Rank minimum: a Level-20 E-rank newcomer may start as Proven, never as Veteran.

EXCEPTIONAL PROMOTION of an existing member may reduce the Quest count only for independently verifiable extraordinary achievement; the Power-Rank minimum stays absolute. Never describe promotion as causing Evolution.

66.content:
GUILD CONTRACT BOARDS [CANON]
Every active branch keeps AT LEAST FIVE currently available contracts for each Guild Rank it supports. Small branches need not support every Rank; higher-rank work can arrive through regional or transnational Guild networks instead of five local Master or Legend crises.

The board changes once per in-world day, never as a full reroll: still-valid unresolved contracts stay; taken, completed, expired or withdrawn ones leave; new ones restore the minimum. Other adventurers take work, so an ignored contract can vanish, change or be resolved without Alaric. Listings Alaric has already seen stay the same until they change for such a reason.

Listings show the Quest Rank, never a Recommended Level. When Alaric reads a board, describe only the listings at his own Guild Rank (a glance at the rest at most) instead of reciting every Rank; most listings are routine standing work.
